question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 120 m and the distance between any two parallel sides is 15 m. The area of the rhombus is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the rhombus = Perimeter ÷ 4

Side = 120 ÷ 4 = 30 m

Area = Base × Height = 30 × 15 = 450 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 450 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Perimeter = 120 m, Height (distance between parallel sides) = 15 m

Formula: Perimeter = 4 × side | Area = side × height

 

 
• 
 

 Base (Side) = 30 m
 Height = 15 m
 Rhombus
 Area = 30 × 15 = 450 m²

⇒ 4 × Side = 120

⇒ Side = 120 ÷ 4 = 30 m

⇒ Area = Side × Height

⇒ Area = 30 × 15

⇒ Area = 450 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 450 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area using Diagonals

The area of a rhombus can also be calculated if diagonals d₁ and d₂ are known: Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂.

Side-Diagonal Relation

The sum of the squares of the diagonals is equal to four times the square of the side: d₁² + d₂² = 4 × side².

Rhombus Properties

A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal. Its diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°).</p
